messages:
maria: heads-up — since ~03:00 UTC we're seeing a spike in 502/handshake errors for eu inference endpoints when clients connect over IPv6. error rate ~4% -> 12% on canary. graphs in #prod-telemetry show it correlated with the new edge LB rollout :confused:
infra-bot: ALERT: service=inference-eu status=Degraded metric=client_errors(https) threshold=5% window=5m
aj: copying. can you paste any failing curl/traceroute/dig outputs?
maria: sure — from an ipv6-only test container (inside region eu-west1):
```
$ curl -6 -v https://inference-eu.redwood.ai/v1/ping
* Trying 2a03:xxxx:abcd::1:443...
* Connected to inference-eu.redwood.ai (2a03:xxxx:abcd::1) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake error: EOF
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) OpenSSL SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in connection to inference-eu.redwood.ai:443 
```

maria: dig output for the service record: 
```
$ dig +short AAAA inference-eu.redwood.ai
2a03:xxxx:abcd::1
```
kevin: i repro'd from an ipv6-only worker behind our NAT64 gateway — it fails fast with TLS handshake too. when i force ipv4 it works fine. looks like the LB advertises an IPv6 but isn't terminating TLS properly on that path.
aj: did we enable dualstack on the new edge LB? configuration diffs?
maria: LB config shows dualstack=true and listener on 443, target group points to ipv4 instance pool via proxy protocol. suspicious. maybe the LB v6 front-end isn't proxying correctly to the ipv4 backend.
nora: if the LB v6 listener isn't doing proper TLS termination or proxying, ipv6 clients will fail. For ipv6-only clients using DNS64/NAT64, if an AAAA exists and points to a broken v6 address they won't fall back to synthesized A -> ipv4 path. removing the AAAA lets DNS64 synthesize an AAAA from the A record and NAT64 will work. quick mitigation: remove AAAA for inference-eu while we fix LB.
kevin: +1 for quick mitigation. we saw similar at another customer where the presence of a bad AAAA killed ipv6-only traffic.
aj: can we flip DNS quickly? what's the TTL?
maria: TTL is 60s for the service record. i can push a change to omit AAAA in the zone and propagate in ~1 min. any objections?
kevin: do it. also open a hotfix ticket to fix the LB listener mapping. i can take the LB config.
nora: i'll add a temporary synthetic IPv6 healthcheck that probes through the LB v6 listener directly so we can validate after fix. also add an alert on handshake errors specifically for ipv6 addresses.
deply-bot: (deploy-bot) rolling back canary: inference-edge-eu canary -> previous config. started 1782123468.
infra-bot: NOTE: removing AAAA will cause some native IPv6 clients (with working LB) to use NAT64 instead, which may slightly increase p99 latency for that subset. tradeoff acceptable for availability.
aj: what are next steps and owners?
maria: 1) DNS change (remove AAAA) — owner: maria — done in ~2m. 2) LB debug + config fix (ensure v6 listener proxies to ipv4 target group or enable ipv6 backend addresses) — owner: kevin — hotfix ticket INFRA-876 open. 3) add v6-focused healthchecks and alerting — owner: nora. 4) postmortem + runbook update for dualstack rollouts — owner: aj.
kevin: I'll dig into target group mapping and TLS handshake logs on the LB. initial hypothesis: the v6 listener was created but its target registration failed due to a cloud provider bug in our IaC module. If true, we need a schema change and a patch to the module.
nora: we'll also add a synthetic test to our chaos suite to validate ipv6-only flows through the edge during canaries.
aj: thanks — will watch metrics and confirm once DNS change propagated. ping me if you need an emergency revert. :thumbsup:
maria: DNS change pushed, AAAA removed from zone. monitoring now.
kevin: i'm seeing ipv6 handshake errors drop in the canary after DNS change; ipv6-only clients are now reaching back via NAT64.
infra-bot: RESOLVED: service=inference-eu status=Degraded -> Healthy. incident window: 1782123456 - 1782123899.
aj: follow-up ticket for runbook and IaC fix in INFRA-876 and a short postmortem. thanks team! :clap:
